channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Manta bridge fees: what deposits and withdrawals cost
item.description: Manta Bridge costs depend on the network transactions behind each transfer. Learn which side charges gas and what to check before you send funds.

item.title: Set a Swap Limit When an Oracle Check Is Missing
item.description: When a swap has no oracle check, set a minimum output from the live quote, then tighten it for price movement without confusing tolerance with fair value.

item.title: Compare Cross-Chain Swap Fees by What You Receive
item.description: Compare cross-chain swap quotes by the amount that arrives, then check broker, network and liquidity costs, execution risk and quote expiry before you trade.

item.title: Chainflip slippage controls give integrators two price limits
item.description: Chainflip integrators can set a quote-based minimum, an oracle-based price limit and a refund deadline, then use the SDK’s quote recommendations to tune each swap.

item.title: What a cross-chain swap really costs
item.description: A cross-chain swap can cost more than its stated fee: source gas, route charges, liquidity and destination payout all shape what reaches your wallet in the end.

item.title: Compare Pool Fee Revenue Across Trading Sessions
item.description: Compare pool fee revenue by matching session windows, normalizing for pool size and time, and separating fees earned from token price changes and incentives.

item.title: How to read tick density before a Solana swap
item.description: Tick density can show where a Solana pool’s liquidity changes, but nearby depth and the route’s expected price impact matter more before you approve a swap.

item.title: Why Token Taxes Throw Off Bridge Estimates
item.description: A token tax can shrink the amount a bridge receives or make a transfer fail, while gas estimates measure execution; check both figures before sending.

item.title: Which Bungee bridge route gets your app the token it needs?
item.description: A Bungee bridge route should be chosen by the destination token and chain your app needs, then checked for asset identity, route steps and final receipt.

item.title: Why Your First Wallet Swap Takes Two Transactions
item.description: A first token swap often needs an approval transaction before the trade; learn what each signature does, when approval repeats, and what to check in your wallet.

item.title: Pool activity and on-chain counts measure different things
item.description: Pool events show what happened inside a trading pool; chain counts show submitted transactions, changing how you read activity, volume and users.

item.title: What Wrong-Network Recovery Can—and Cannot—Do
item.description: Wrong-network recovery depends on where the funds landed and who controls the receiving address; check the transaction first, then choose the right recovery path.

item.title: How to Rebalance After a Partial LP Withdrawal
item.description: After a partial LP withdrawal, check the assets you received, choose a target mix, and swap only the amount needed before adding liquidity again.

item.title: Impermanent loss: what to check before providing liquidity
item.description: Impermanent loss can leave a liquidity provider with less value than simply holding the tokens. Compare price risk, fees and pool terms before you deposit.

item.title: Why USDT Transfers Need Different TRON Energy
item.description: USDT transfers on TRON use Energy to run the token contract, and the receiver’s USDT balance can change the amount needed for a send. Check resources first.

item.title: Rent or Stake Energy for USDT Transfers on TRON?
item.description: For occasional USDT transfers on TRON, renting delegated Energy can avoid locking TRX; frequent users may prefer staking, while burn fees offer a simple fallback.

item.title: What Bandwidth and Energy do in a TRON USDT transfer
item.description: A TRON USDT transfer uses Bandwidth for transaction data and Energy for its token contract, so the sender's resources and recipient's token balance shape the fee.

item.title: Tron Energy: Rent, Stake or Pay in TRX?
item.description: Tron Energy can cut the TRX burned on USDT transfers, but renting, staking and paying the network suit different habits, transfer patterns and wallet balances.

item.title: Three ways to set XMR-to-Bitcoin confirmation rules
item.description: XMR-to-Bitcoin swaps can settle after a first block, a fixed wait, or a value-based threshold, each trading payout speed against the risk of a chain reversal.

item.title: Monero swap pending? Check these details before retrying
item.description: A pending Monero swap may still be processing. Check the original transaction and order details before retrying to avoid sending a second deposit.
